transcript.content: Hello, welcome in. What brings you to see me today?
I came in because my eating has been really off for months. Some days I barely eat—just toast and coffee—and other days I end up buying sweets I don’t even really enjoy.
During those times when you eat the sweets, do you feel like you are unable to stop or control how much you eat?
I’m not really sure. I do buy them sometimes, but I haven’t noticed that I can’t stop once I start.
Do you have an intense fear of gaining weight or becoming fat?
No, I don’t think so. I haven’t been particularly afraid of gaining weight.
Over the past few months, have you been feeling persistently down, sad, or hopeless?
Yes. Most days I wake up feeling this heavy sadness. Even when I’m in my bright kitchen making coffee, it feels like the warmth has gone out of everything.
Have you ever experienced a period of feeling down or depressed like this in the past, before these last few months?
Yes. It’s been going on about seven months now, since my aunt came to live with me after her fall.
Have you lost interest or pleasure in things you usually enjoy doing?
Yes. I used to enjoy quilting, bowling night, and planning potlucks. Now I look at my quilting supplies or the church calendar and just... I can’t make myself care about it the way I used to.
How has your sleep been during this time?
I’m not really sure what to say about my sleep. I haven’t paid much attention to it, I guess.
Have you been feeling unusually tired or lacking in energy most days?
Yes. Even on a night when my aunt doesn’t call out and I sleep through, I’m worn down by breakfast. Carrying laundry or even making phone calls feels like it takes more out of me than it should.
Have you noticed any trouble concentrating, focusing, or making everyday decisions lately?
I’m not sure. I haven’t really noticed any particular problems with that.
Have you been struggling with feelings of worthlessness or excessive guilt lately?
I guess so. People at church say I’m doing fine, but I can’t shake the feeling everybody in Manawa knows I’m letting my aunt down. Like they’re all whispering about what a burden I’ve become.
Have you ever had a period of time where you felt the opposite—unusually energetic, hyper, or on top of the world, needing very little sleep?
No, I don’t think I’ve had a time like that. I can’t recall feeling unusually energized or needing hardly any sleep.

inference_history.note: Initial differential based on patient reporting months of disordered eating alternating between restriction and compulsive eating of sweets, which could represent an eating disorder or an underlying depressive episode.
Ruled out F50.0 (Anorexia nervosa) and F50.2 (Bulimia nervosa) due to denial of fear of gaining weight and lack of clear loss-of-control binge eating.
